title: Poly1305 one-time MAC
summary: Poly1305 is a one-time MAC (RFC 8439) that authenticates a message using a 256-bit one-time key. The key is split into r (128 bits, clamped) and s (128 bits). The message is processed in 16-byte blocks, each interpreted as a little-endian integer and multiplied by r modulo 2^130-5. The final tag is (accumulator + s) mod 2^128.

structure.meaning: r (16 bytes, clamped: r &= 0x0ffffffc0ffffffc0ffffffc0fffffff) + s (16 bytes).
Each 16-byte chunk interpreted as a little-endian integer, with a 0x01 byte appended (for the final partial block, pad with zeros then 0x01).

ext.example_decoded: Poly1305 one-time key (all zeros, for illustration)
notes: Poly1305 is always used with a nonce-based cipher (ChaCha20, AES) to derive the one-time key.
The clamping of r ensures the multiplication is safe (no carry overflow).
ChaCha20-Poly1305 is the AEAD used by TLS 1.3, WireGuard, and SSH.
